source: Team demo content from the gap analysis (B-3), based on NASA HRP risks 'Altered sensorimotor and vestibular function' and 'Injury from dynamic loads'; not medical advice; needs flight-surgeon review

questions.text: Did this start after landing or a gravity change?
Did they lose consciousness, even for a moment?
How are they when lying down?

answers.label: Confused, or cannot sit up at all

summary.LOW: Mild dizziness from moving. Rest and let the body adapt.
summary.MODERATE: Strong dizziness. Keep them lying down and watch them closely.
summary.CRITICAL: They fainted or are getting worse. Protect the airway and alert the base.

LOW.text: Help them lie down and rest.
Look at one fixed point. Move the head slowly.
Give fluids if they feel well enough.

MODERATE.text: Give fluids if they are awake.
Check heart rate on the vitals screen.
Alert the base if they are not better in 15 minutes.

CRITICAL.text: Lay them on their side and keep the airway open.
Check breathing and heart rate on the vitals screen.
Do not let them stand up.
Stay with them until help arrives.

callBaseWhen: Call the base if they faint again or do not improve lying down.
